title.zh: 卷三百二十七 列傳第二百十五 外國八 韃靼
title.raw: 卷三百二十七 列傳第二百十五 外國八 韃靼 Volume 327 Biographies 215: Foreign States 8

sentences.zh: 韃靼，即蒙古，故元後也。

translations.literal: The Tartars are the Mongols, the remnant of the former Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Tartars were the Mongols—the surviving remnant of the Yuan dynasty.

sentences.zh: 太祖洪武元年，大將軍徐達率師取元，元主自北平遁出塞，居開平，數遣其將也速等擾北邊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongwu, the Taizu, Great General Xu Da led troops to take the Yuan; the Yuan emperor fled from Beiping out beyond the passes, dwelt at Kaiping, and repeatedly sent his generals Yesu and others to harass the northern border.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Hongwu, the Hongwu Emperor dispatched the great general Xu Da to conquer the Yuan. The Yuan emperor fled Beiping for the lands beyond the frontier and made his seat at Kaiping, from which he repeatedly sent generals such as Yesu to raid the northern border.

sentences.zh: 明年，常遇春擊敗之，師進開平，俘宗王慶孫、平章鼎住。

translations.literal: The next year, Chang Yuchun defeated them; the army advanced to Kaiping and captured the imperial prince Qingsun and the Pingzhang Dingzhu.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Chang Yuchun routed the Yuan forces and pressed on to Kaiping, where he took captive the imperial prince Qingsun and the minister Dingzhu.

sentences.zh: 時元主奔應昌，其將王保保據定西為邊患。

translations.literal: At this time the Yuan emperor fled to Yingchang; his general Wang Baobao held Dingxi and became a border menace.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Yuan emperor had fled to Yingchang, while his general Wang Baobao held Dingxi and became a persistent threat along the frontier.

sentences.zh: 三年春，以徐達為大將軍，使出西安搗定西；

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year, Xu Da was made great general and ordered to set out from Xi'an and strike at Dingxi;
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year Xu Da was appointed great general and ordered to march from Xi'an against Dingxi;

sentences.zh: 李文忠為左副將軍，馮勝為右副將軍，使出居庸搗應昌。

translations.literal: Li Wenzhong was made left deputy general and Feng Sheng right deputy general, and ordered to set out from Juyong and strike at Yingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wenzhong was named left deputy general and Feng Sheng right deputy general, with orders to advance through Juyong Pass and strike at Yingchang.

sentences.zh: 文忠至興和，擒平章竹貞，復大破元兵於駱駝山，遂趨應昌。

translations.literal: Wenzhong reached Xinghe, captured the Pingzhang Zhuzhen, again greatly defeated Yuan troops at Camel Mountain, and then hastened toward Yingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong reached Xinghe, captured the minister Zhuzhen, won a great victory over Yuan forces at Camel Mountain, and pressed on toward Yingchang.

sentences.zh: 未至，知元主已殂，進圍其城，克之。

translations.literal: Before arriving, he learned that the Yuan emperor had already died; he advanced to besiege the city and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived he learned that the Yuan emperor was already dead. He advanced, besieged the city, and took it.

sentences.zh: 獲元主孫買的裡八剌及其妃嬪、大臣、寶玉、圖籍。

translations.literal: He captured the Yuan emperor's grandson Maidiribala, along with his consorts, ministers, precious jades, and archives.
translations.idiomatic: Among the spoils were the Yuan emperor's grandson Maidiribala, the imperial consorts, court ministers, precious jades, and the dynastic archives.

sentences.zh: 太子愛猷識理達臘獨以數十騎遁去。

translations.literal: The crown prince Ayushiridara alone escaped with several dozen horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Only the crown prince Ayushiridara escaped, fleeing with a few dozen horsemen.

sentences.zh: 而徐達亦大破王保保兵於沈兒峪口，走之。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Xu Da also greatly defeated Wang Baobao's army at Shen'er Pass and put them to flight.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Xu Da won a crushing victory over Wang Baobao's army at Shen'er Pass and drove him from the field.

sentences.zh: 太祖封買的裡八剌為崇禮侯，謚元主曰順帝。

translations.literal: The Taizu enfeoffed Maidiribala as Marquis Chongli and gave the Yuan emperor the posthumous title Emperor Shun.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongwu Emperor enfeoffed Maidiribala as Marquis Chongli and granted the Yuan emperor the posthumous title Emperor Shun.

sentences.zh: 於是故元諸將江文清等、王子失篤兒等，先後歸附。

translations.literal: Thereupon the former Yuan generals Jiang Wenqing and others, and princes Shidur and others, successively submitted.
translations.idiomatic: After this, former Yuan generals such as Jiang Wenqing and princes such as Shidur submitted to the Ming one after another.

sentences.zh: 獨王保保擁太子愛猷識理達臘居和林，屢詔諭之，不從。

translations.literal: Only Wang Baobao, holding the crown prince Ayushiridara, dwelt at Karakorum; edicts repeatedly admonished him, but he would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Only Wang Baobao, holding the crown prince Ayushiridara at Karakorum, defied repeated imperial edicts and refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 五年春，命大將軍徐達、左副將軍李文忠、征西將軍馮勝率師三道征之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year, the great general Xu Da, left deputy general Li Wenzhong, and western campaign general Feng Sheng were ordered to lead troops in three columns to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year the court ordered the great general Xu Da, left deputy general Li Wenzhong, and western campaign general Feng Sheng to march against them in three columns.

sentences.zh: 大將軍達由中路出雁門，戰不利，守塞。

translations.literal: The great general Da set out by the central route through Yanmen; the battle went badly, and he held the passes.
translations.idiomatic: The great general Xu Da marched by the central route through Yanmen Pass, fought without success, and held the frontier defenses.

sentences.zh: 勝軍西次蘭州。

translations.literal: Sheng's army halted in the west at Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Sheng's army encamped in the west at Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 右副將軍傅友德先進，轉戰至埽林山，勝等兵合，斬其平章不花，降上都驢等所部吏民八千三百餘戶，遂由亦集乃路至瓜、沙州，復連敗之。

translations.literal: Right deputy general Fu Youde advanced first, fought in succession to Saolin Mountain; Sheng and the others joined forces, beheaded their Pingzhang Buhua, accepted the surrender of more than eight thousand three hundred households of officials and people under Shangdu Lu and others, then went by way of Ejin to Guazhou and Shazhou, and again defeated them in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Right deputy general Fu Youde led the advance, fighting his way to Saolin Mountain, where Feng Sheng joined him. They beheaded the minister Buhua and accepted the surrender of more than eight thousand three hundred households under Shangdu Lu and his followers. Then, marching by way of Ejin to Guazhou and Shazhou, they won victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 文忠東出居庸至口溫，元將棄營遁，乃率輕騎自臚朐河疾馳，進敗蠻子哈剌章於土剌河，追及阿魯渾河，又追及稱海，獲其官屬子孫並軍士家屬千八百餘，送京師。

translations.literal: Wenzhong set out east from Juyong to Kouwen; the Yuan generals abandoned their camp and fled. He then led light cavalry in a swift dash from the Luqu River, advanced and defeated Manzi Halazhang at the Tula River, pursued to the Arun River, and pursued again to Chenghai, capturing more than eighteen hundred of their officials, descendants, and soldiers' families, and sent them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong marched east from Juyong Pass to Kouwen, where the Yuan generals abandoned their camp and fled. He then led light cavalry in a swift dash from the Luqu River, routed Manzi Halazhang on the Tula River, pursued the enemy to the Arun River and then to Chenghai, and captured more than eighteen hundred officials, their kin, and soldiers' families, whom he sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 達等尋召還。

translations.literal: Da and the others were soon recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da and the other commanders were soon recalled.

sentences.zh: 明年春，遣達、文忠等備西北邊。

translations.literal: In the spring of the next year, Da, Wenzhong, and others were dispatched to guard the northwestern border.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring Xu Da, Wenzhong, and others were dispatched to guard the northwestern frontier.

sentences.zh: 元兵入犯武、朔，達遣陳德、郭子興擊破之。

translations.literal: Yuan troops entered and invaded Wu and Shuo; Da sent Chen De and Guo Zixing to defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan forces invaded Wu and Shuo, Xu Da sent Chen De and Guo Zixing to repulse them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，達等復大破王保保兵於懷柔。

translations.literal: Before long, Da and the others again greatly defeated Wang Baobao's army at Huairou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xu Da and his colleagues won another great victory over Wang Baobao's army at Huairou.

sentences.zh: 時元兵先後犯白登、保德、河曲，輒為守將所敗，獨撫寧、瑞州被殘，太祖乃徙其民於內地。

translations.literal: At this time Yuan troops successively invaded Baideng, Baode, and Hequ, and were each time defeated by the defending generals; only Funing and Ruizhou were ravaged, whereupon the Taizu relocated their people to the interior.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan raids against Baideng, Baode, and Hequ were beaten back one after another, but Funing and Ruizhou were devastated. The Hongwu Emperor therefore relocated their people to safer lands within the interior.

sentences.zh: 七年夏，都督藍玉拔興和。

translations.literal: In the summer of the seventh year, the commander Lan Yu captured Xinghe.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the seventh year the commander Lan Yu took Xinghe.

sentences.zh: 文忠亦遣裨將擒斬其長，而自以大軍攻高州大石崖，克之，斬宗王、大臣朵朵失裡等，至氈帽山斬魯王，獲其妃蒙哥禿。

translations.literal: Wenzhong also sent a subordinate general to capture and behead their chief, while he himself led the main army to attack the Great Stone Cliff of Gaozhou, took it, beheaded the imperial prince and minister Duoduoshili and others, reached Zhanmao Mountain and beheaded the Prince of Lu, and captured his consort Menggutu.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong sent a subordinate general to capture and behead an enemy chieftain, while he himself led the main army against the Great Stone Cliff of Gaozhou and took it. There he executed the imperial prince Duoduoshili and other ministers, then pressed on to Zhanmao Mountain, where he killed the Prince of Lu and captured his consort Menggutu.

sentences.zh: 秋，太祖以故元太子流離沙漠，父子隔絕，未有後嗣，乃遣崇禮侯北歸，以書諭之。

translations.literal: In autumn, because the former Yuan crown prince was wandering in the desert, father and son were separated, and there was no heir, the Taizu sent the Marquis Chongli north to return home and admonished him by letter.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, moved by the plight of the former Yuan crown prince—exiled in the desert, cut off from his father, and without an heir—the Hongwu Emperor sent the Marquis Chongli back north with a letter of admonition.

sentences.zh: 又二年，其部下九住等寇西邊，敗去。

translations.literal: Two years later, his subordinates Jiuzhu and others raided the western border and were defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later his followers Jiuzhu and others raided the western frontier, were defeated, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 洪武十一年夏，故元太子愛猷識理達臘卒，太祖自為文，遣使弔祭。

translations.literal: In the summer of the eleventh year of Hongwu, the former Yuan crown prince Ayushiridara died; the Taizu personally composed the text and sent envoys to offer condolences and sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the eleventh year of Hongwu the former Yuan crown prince Ayushiridara died. The Hongwu Emperor composed the eulogy himself and sent envoys to mourn and sacrifice on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 子脫古思帖木兒繼立。

translations.literal: His son Toghus Temür succeeded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: His son Toghus Temür succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 其丞相驢兒、蠻子哈剌章，國公脫火赤，平章完者不花、乃兒不花，樞密知院愛足等，擁眾於應昌、和林，時出沒塞下。

translations.literal: Their chancellor Lu'er, Manzi Halazhang, the state duke Tuohuochi, the Pingzhang Wanzhebuhua and Na'erbuhua, the Privy Council vice-director Aizu, and others gathered followers at Yingchang and Karakorum and at times appeared and vanished below the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Their chancellor Lu'er, Manzi Halazhang, the state duke Tuohuochi, the ministers Wanzhebuhua and Na'erbuhua, the Privy Council vice-director Aizu, and others gathered forces at Yingchang and Karakorum, raiding back and forth along the frontier.

sentences.zh: 太祖屢賜璽書諭之，不從。

translations.literal: The Taizu repeatedly sent sealed edicts to admonish them, but they would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongwu Emperor repeatedly sent sealed edicts urging submission, but they refused to heed him.

sentences.zh: 十三年春，西平侯沐英師出靈州，渡黃河，歷賀蘭山，踐流沙，擒脫火赤、愛足等於和林，盡以其部曲歸。

translations.literal: In the spring of the thirteenth year, the Marquis of Xiping Mu Ying's army set out from Lingzhou, crossed the Yellow River, passed Helan Mountain, trod the drifting sands, captured Tuohuochi, Aizu, and others at Karakorum, and brought all their followers back.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the thirteenth year the Marquis of Xiping Mu Ying marched from Lingzhou, crossed the Yellow River, crossed Helan Mountain and the drifting sands, captured Tuohuochi, Aizu, and others at Karakorum, and brought all their followers back with him.

sentences.zh: 冬，完者不花亦就擒。

translations.literal: In winter, Wanzhebuhua was also captured.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Wanzhebuhua was captured as well.

sentences.zh: 明年春，徐達及副將軍湯和、傅友德征乃兒不花，至河北，襲灰山，斬獲甚眾。

translations.literal: In the spring of the next year, Xu Da and deputy generals Tang He and Fu Youde campaigned against Na'erbuhua, reached Hebei, raided Huishan Mountain, and killed and captured a great many.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring Xu Da, with deputy generals Tang He and Fu Youde, marched against Na'erbuhua, reached Hebei, struck Huishan Mountain, and killed or captured a great many of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 時王保保已先卒，諸巨魁多以次平定，或望風歸附，獨丞相納哈出擁二十萬眾據金山，數窺伺遼。

translations.literal: At this time Wang Baobao had already died first; the great chieftains were for the most part pacified in turn, or submitted at the mere sight of Ming forces—only Chancellor Nahachu, holding two hundred thousand followers at Jinshan, repeatedly watched for an opportunity to raid Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: By then Wang Baobao was already dead, and most of the great chieftains had been subdued in turn or submitted at the first sight of Ming banners. Only Chancellor Nahachu, holding two hundred thousand men at Jinshan, repeatedly watched for a chance to strike into Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 二十年春，命宋國公馮勝為大將軍，率潁川侯傅友德、永昌侯藍玉等，將兵二十萬征之，還其先所獲元將乃剌吾。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twentieth year, the Duke of Song Feng Sheng was made great general and, leading the Marquis of Yingchuan Fu Youde, the Marquis of Yongchang Lan Yu, and others, commanded two hundred thousand troops to campaign against him; they also returned the former Yuan general Nalaiwu whom they had previously captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twentieth year Feng Sheng, Duke of Song, was appointed great general. At the head of two hundred thousand men—including Fu Youde, Marquis of Yingchuan, and Lan Yu, Marquis of Yongchang—he marched against Nahachu, bringing with him the former Yuan general Nalaiwu, whom the Ming had captured earlier and now returned.

sentences.zh: 勝軍駐通州，遣藍玉乘大雪襲慶州，克之。

translations.literal: Sheng's army encamped at Tongzhou and sent Lan Yu to exploit the heavy snow and raid Qingzhou, which was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Sheng encamped at Tongzhou and sent Lan Yu to exploit a heavy snowfall and storm Qingzhou, which fell.

sentences.zh: 夏，師逾金山，臨江侯陳鏞失道，陷敵死。

translations.literal: In summer the army crossed Jinshan; the Marquis of Linjiang Chen Yong lost his way, fell into the enemy, and died.
translations.idiomatic: That summer the army crossed Jinshan. Chen Yong, Marquis of Linjiang, lost his way, was cut off by the enemy, and killed.

sentences.zh: 乃剌吾歸，備以朝廷撫卹恩語其眾，於是全國公觀童來降。

translations.literal: When Nalaiwu returned, he explained to his followers the court's benevolent care; thereupon the state duke Guantong came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Nalaiwu returned, he told his followers of the court's benevolent treatment, and the state duke Guantong came over to the Ming.

sentences.zh: 納哈出因聞乃剌吾之言已心悸，復為大軍所迫，乃陽使人至大將軍營納款，以覘兵勢。

translations.literal: Nahachu, having heard Nalaiwu's words, was already apprehensive at heart; pressed again by the main army, he feigned submission by sending men to the great general's camp to offer allegiance and spy on the army's strength.
translations.idiomatic: Nahachu, shaken by Nalaiwu's report and hard pressed by the main army, feigned submission, sending envoys to the great general's camp to offer allegiance while spying on Ming strength.

sentences.zh: 勝遣玉往受降。

translations.literal: Sheng dispatched Yu to go and accept the surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Sheng sent Lan Yu to receive the surrender.

sentences.zh: 使者見勝軍還報，納哈出仰天嘆曰：「天弗使吾有此眾矣。

translations.literal: When the envoys saw Sheng's army and returned to report, Nahachu looked up to heaven and sighed, saying: "Heaven will not let me keep this host."
translations.idiomatic: When his envoys saw Feng Sheng's army and returned to report, Nahachu looked up to heaven and sighed: "Heaven will not let me keep this host."

sentences.zh: 」遂率數百騎詣玉納降。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led several hundred horsemen to Yu to submit.
translations.idiomatic: He then rode with several hundred men to Lan Yu and submitted.

sentences.zh: 已，將脫去，為鄭國公常茂所傷不得去。

translations.literal: Soon after, when he was about to slip away, he was wounded by the Duke of Zheng Chang Mao and could not escape.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, as he tried to slip away, Chang Mao, Duke of Zheng, wounded him and prevented his escape.

sentences.zh: 都督耿忠遂以眾擁之見勝，勝重禮之，使忠與同寢食。

translations.literal: The commander Geng Zhong then led the troops to escort him before Sheng; Sheng treated him with great courtesy and had Zhong eat and sleep with him.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Geng Zhong then escorted him before Feng Sheng, who received him with great courtesy and had Zhong share his meals and lodging.

sentences.zh: 先後降其部曲二十餘萬人，及聞納哈出傷，由是驚潰者四萬人，獲輜重畜馬亙百餘里。

translations.literal: Before and after, more than two hundred thousand of his followers submitted; when they heard that Nahachu had been wounded, forty thousand more panicked and fled. Baggage, livestock, and horses stretched for more than a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: More than two hundred thousand of his followers submitted in the course of the campaign. When word spread that Nahachu had been wounded, another forty thousand panicked and fled, abandoning baggage, livestock, and horses that stretched along the road for more than a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 勝班師，都督濮英以三千騎殿，為潰卒所邀襲，死之。

translations.literal: Sheng withdrew the army; the commander Pu Ying, with three thousand horsemen as rearguard, was intercepted and ambushed by fleeing soldiers and died.
translations.idiomatic: As Feng Sheng withdrew, Commander Pu Ying, covering the retreat with three thousand horsemen, was ambushed by fleeing soldiers and killed.

sentences.zh: 秋，勝等表上納哈出所部官屬二百餘人，將校三千三百餘人，金銀銅印一百顆，虎符牌面百二十五事，馬二百九十餘匹， 稱賀。

translations.literal: In autumn, Sheng and the others memorialized the more than two hundred officials of Nahachu's following, more than three thousand three hundred officers, one hundred gold, silver, and bronze seals, one hundred twenty-five tiger tallies and command plaques, more than two hundred ninety horses, and offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Feng Sheng and his colleagues memorialized the capture of more than two hundred officials from Nahachu's following, more than three thousand three hundred officers, one hundred gold, silver, and bronze seals, one hundred twenty-five tiger tallies and command plaques, and more than two hundred ninety horses, offering congratulations on the victory.

sentences.zh: 太祖封納哈出為海西侯，先後賜予甚厚，並授乃剌吾千戶。

translations.literal: The Taizu enfeoffed Nahachu as Marquis of Haixi and richly rewarded him before and after, also granting Nalaiwu the rank of chiliarch.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongwu Emperor enfeoffed Nahachu as Marquis of Haixi, lavished rewards upon him, and granted Nalaiwu the rank of chiliarch.

sentences.zh: 納哈出既降，帝以故元遺寇終為邊患，乃即軍中拜藍玉為大將軍，唐勝、郭英副之，耿忠、孫恪為左、右參將，率師十五萬往征之。

translations.literal: After Nahachu had submitted, the emperor, considering that remnant Yuan raiders would ultimately remain a border menace, immediately in the army appointed Lan Yu as great general, with Tang Sheng and Guo Ying as deputies and Geng Zhong and Sun Ke as left and right staff generals, and ordered them to lead one hundred fifty thousand troops to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Once Nahachu had submitted, the emperor—fearing that remnant Yuan bands would remain a lasting frontier menace—promoted Lan Yu to great general on the spot, with Tang Sheng and Guo Ying as deputies and Geng Zhong and Sun Ke as left and right staff generals, and sent them north with one hundred fifty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 冬，元將脫脫等降於玉。

translations.literal: In winter, the Yuan generals Tuotuo and others submitted to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Yuan generals Tuotuo and others submitted to Lan Yu.

sentences.zh: 明年春，玉以大軍由大寧至慶州，聞脫古思帖木兒在捕魚兒海，從間道馳進，至百眼井哨不見敵，欲引還。

translations.literal: In the spring of the next year, Yu led the main army from Daning to Qingzhou; hearing that Toghus Temür was at Buyur Lake, he hurried by a hidden route and, reaching the Baiyanjing outpost without seeing the enemy, wished to turn back.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring Lan Yu led the main army from Daning to Qingzhou. Hearing that Toghus Temür was encamped at Buyur Lake, he hurried along a hidden route. When he reached the Baiyanjing outpost and still saw no enemy, he wished to turn back.

sentences.zh: 定遠侯王弼曰：「吾等奉聖主威德，提十萬餘眾，深入至此，無所得，何以覆命？

translations.literal: The Marquis of Dingyuan Wang Bi said: "We have come bearing the august sovereign's majesty and virtue, leading more than one hundred thousand men, penetrating this far—if we gain nothing, how shall we answer for our mission?"
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Dingyuan, Wang Bi, said: "We march under the Son of Heaven's majesty at the head of more than one hundred thousand men. Having come this deep into enemy country, how can we return empty-handed?"

sentences.zh: 」玉乃穴地而爨，一夜馳至捕魚兒海。

translations.literal: Yu then dug pits in the earth to cook and, in one night, galloped to Buyur Lake.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Yu then dug cooking pits in the earth and, in a single night, galloped on to Buyur Lake.

sentences.zh: 黎明，去敵營八十里。

translations.literal: At dawn they were eighty li from the enemy camp.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they were eighty li from the enemy camp.

sentences.zh: 時大風揚沙，晝晦，軍行無知者，敵不設備。

translations.literal: At that time a great wind raised the sand; daylight was dim; the army marched without being detected, and the enemy made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: A great wind whipped up the sand and blotted out the daylight. The army advanced unseen, and the enemy stood unprepared.

sentences.zh: 弼為前鋒，直薄之，遂大破其軍，斬太尉、蠻子數千人。

translations.literal: Bi served as vanguard and pressed straight upon them; thereupon the army was greatly broken, and the Grand Preceptor Manzi and several thousand others were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bi led the vanguard and struck straight at the enemy camp. The Yuan army was shattered, and the Grand Preceptor Manzi and several thousand others were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 脫古思帖木兒以其太子天保奴、知院捏怯來、丞相失烈門等數十騎遁去，獲其次子地保奴及妃主五十餘人、渠率三千、男女七萬餘，馬駝牛羊十萬，聚鎧仗焚之。

translations.literal: Toghus Temür escaped with his crown prince Tianbaonu, the vice-director Nieqilai, the chancellor Shiliemen, and several dozen horsemen; they captured his second son Dibaonu and more than fifty consorts and princesses, three thousand chieftains, more than seventy thousand men and women, one hundred thousand horses, camels, cattle, and sheep, gathered the armor and weapons, and burned them.
translations.idiomatic: Toghus Temür fled with his crown prince Tianbaonu, the vice-director Nieqilai, the chancellor Shiliemen, and a few dozen horsemen. The Ming captured his second son Dibaonu, more than fifty consorts and princesses, three thousand chieftains, more than seventy thousand men and women, and one hundred thousand horses, camels, cattle, and sheep; they piled up the captured armor and weapons and burned them.

sentences.zh: 又破其將哈剌章營，盡降其眾。

translations.literal: They again broke the camp of his general Halazhang and wholly accepted the surrender of his followers.
translations.idiomatic: They then broke the camp of his general Halazhang and accepted the surrender of all his followers.

sentences.zh: 於是漠北削平。

translations.literal: Thereupon the northern desert was leveled.
translations.idiomatic: With that, the northern desert was brought to heel.

sentences.zh: 捷奏至，太祖大悅，賜地保奴等鈔幣，命有司給供具。

translations.literal: When the victory report arrived, the Taizu was greatly pleased and bestowed paper money on Dibaonu and the others, ordering the relevant offices to provide supplies.
translations.idiomatic: When news of the victory arrived, the Hongwu Emperor was greatly pleased. He bestowed paper money on Dibaonu and the others and ordered the relevant offices to provide for them.

sentences.zh: 既有言玉私元主妃者，帝怒，妃慚懼自殺。

translations.literal: When someone reported that Yu had privately taken a consort of the Yuan emperor, the emperor was angry; the consort, ashamed and fearful, killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Lan Yu had privately taken a consort of the Yuan emperor, the emperor flew into a rage. The consort, shamed and terrified, took her own life.

sentences.zh: 地保奴出怨言，帝居之琉球。

translations.literal: Dibaonu uttered resentful words; the emperor had him settled in Ryukyu.
translations.idiomatic: Dibaonu spoke resentfully, and the emperor had him settled in Ryukyu.

sentences.zh: 脫古思帖木兒既遁，將依丞相咬住於和林，行至土剌河，為其下也速迭兒所襲，眾復散，獨與捏怯來等十六騎偕。

translations.literal: After Toghus Temür had fled, he was about to rely on the chancellor Yaoqia at Karakorum; when he reached the Tula River he was attacked by his subordinate Yesudier; his followers again scattered, and he alone remained with Nieqilai and sixteen horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: After his flight Toghus Temür meant to take refuge with Chancellor Yaoqia at Karakorum. On the Tula River his subordinate Yesudier attacked him; his followers scattered again, and only Nieqilai and sixteen horsemen remained at his side.

sentences.zh: 適咬住來迎，欲共往依闊闊帖木兒，大雪不得發。

translations.literal: Just then Yaoqia came to meet him; they intended together to go and rely on Kuokuotemür, but heavy snow prevented them from setting out.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoqia came out to meet him, and they planned to seek refuge with Kuokuotemür, but heavy snow kept them from marching.

sentences.zh: 也速迭兒兵猝至，縊殺之，並殺天保奴。

translations.literal: Yesudier's troops suddenly arrived, strangled him to death, and also killed Tianbaonu.
translations.idiomatic: Yesudier's troops suddenly arrived, strangled Toghus Temür to death, and killed Tianbaonu as well.

sentences.zh: 於是捏怯來、失烈門等來降，置之全寧衛。

translations.literal: Thereupon Nieqilai, Shiliemen, and others came to submit and were settled in the Quanning Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Nieqilai, Shiliemen, and others then submitted and were settled in the Quanning Guard.

sentences.zh: 未幾，捏怯來為失烈門所襲殺，眾潰，詔朵顏等衛招撫之，來降者益眾。

translations.literal: Before long, Nieqilai was attacked and killed by Shiliemen; the host dispersed. An edict ordered the Duoyan and other guards to win them over, and those who came to submit grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Nieqilai was attacked and killed by Shiliemen, and the host broke apart. The court ordered the Duoyan Guard and others to win over the fugitives, and ever more came over to the Ming.

sentences.zh: 二十三年春，命潁國公傅友德等以北平兵從燕王，定遠侯王弼等以山西兵從晉王，征咬住及乃兒不花、阿魯帖木兒等。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-third year, Fu Youde, Duke of Ying, and others were ordered to lead Beiping troops with the Prince of Yan, and Wang Bi, Marquis of Dingyuan, and others to lead Shanxi troops with the Prince of Jin, to campaign against Yaoqia, Na'erbuhua, Aru Timur, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twenty-third year Fu Youde, Duke of Ying, was ordered to lead Beiping troops with the Prince of Yan, and Wang Bi, Marquis of Dingyuan, to lead Shanxi troops with the Prince of Jin, in a campaign against Yaoqia, Na'erbuhua, Aru Timur, and others.

sentences.zh: 燕王出古北口，偵知乃兒不花營迤都，冒大雪馳進，去敵一磧，敵不知也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan set out through the Gubeikou pass; scouts learned that Na'erbuhua's camp was at Yidu; braving the heavy snow he galloped forward, and when he was one stretch of desert from the enemy, they did not know it.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan marched out through Gubeikou. Scouts reported Na'erbuhua's camp at Yidu. He pressed forward through driving snow and, when still one stretch of desert from the enemy, remained undetected.

sentences.zh: 先遣指揮觀童往，觀童舊與乃兒不花善，一見相持泣。

translations.literal: He first sent the commander Guan Tong ahead; Guan Tong had formerly been on good terms with Na'erbuhua, and when they met the two embraced each other and wept.
translations.idiomatic: He first sent Commander Guan Tong ahead. Guan Tong had once been on good terms with Na'erbuhua, and when they met the two embraced and wept.

sentences.zh: 頃之，大軍壓其營，乃兒不花驚，欲遁，觀童止之，引見王，賜飲食慰諭遣還。

translations.literal: Before long the main army pressed upon their camp; Na'erbuhua was alarmed and wished to flee, but Guan Tong stopped him and led him to see the prince, who granted him food and drink, consoled him, and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the main army closed on the camp. Na'erbuhua, startled, tried to flee, but Guan Tong restrained him and brought him before the prince, who feasted him, reassured him, and sent him back.

sentences.zh: 乃兒不花喜過望，遂偕咬住等來降。

translations.literal: Na'erbuhua was delighted beyond expectation and then came to submit together with Yaoqia and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Na'erbuhua, delighted beyond all expectation, then came to submit together with Yaoqia and the others.

sentences.zh: 久之，乃兒不花等以謀叛誅死，敵益衰。

translations.literal: After a long time, Na'erbuhua and the others were executed for plotting rebellion, and the enemy grew ever weaker.
translations.idiomatic: In time Na'erbuhua and his companions were executed for plotting rebellion, and Yuan power on the steppe waned further.

sentences.zh: 太祖亦封燕、晉諸王為邊籓鎮，更歲遣大將巡行塞下，督諸衛卒屯田，戒以持重，寇來輒敗之。

translations.literal: The Taizu also enfeoffed the princes of Yan and Jin as frontier feudatories, and each year dispatched great generals to patrol below the passes, supervising the garrison troops in frontier farming, admonishing them to act with caution, and whenever raiders came, to defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongwu Emperor also enfeoffed the princes of Yan and Jin as frontier lords, sent great generals each year to patrol the northern defenses, supervised garrison troops in frontier farming, and enjoined them to stand firm—whenever raiders came, to beat them back.

sentences.zh: 而敵自脫古思帖木兒後，部帥紛拏，五傳至坤帖木兒，咸被弒，不復知帝號。

translations.literal: But after Toghus Temür, the tribal chiefs were in turmoil; through five successions to Kuntemür, all were assassinated, and they no longer knew the imperial title.
translations.idiomatic: After Toghus Temür the tribal chiefs fell into turmoil. Five rulers succeeded one another down to Kuntemür; each was assassinated, and the steppe no longer even preserved the imperial title.

sentences.zh: 有鬼力赤者篡立，稱可汗，去國號，遂稱韃靼雲。

translations.literal: There was one Güilüchi who usurped the throne, called himself khan, cast off the dynastic name, and thereafter called the realm Tartar Cloud.
translations.idiomatic: One Güilüchi seized power, proclaimed himself khan, cast off the dynastic name, and thereafter styled the realm Tartar Cloud.

sentences.zh: 永樂三年，頭目埽胡兒、察罕達魯花等先後來歸。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongle, the chieftains Saohu'er, Chahandaulihua, and others successively came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongle the chieftains Saohu'er, Chahandaulihua, and others came over to the Ming one after another.

sentences.zh: 久之，阿魯台殺鬼力赤，而迎元之後本雅失裡於別失八里，立為可汗。

translations.literal: After a long time, Arughtai killed Güilüchi and welcomed a descendant of the Yuan, Buyanshir, at Beshbalik, establishing him as khan.
translations.idiomatic: In time Arughtai killed Güilüchi and, at Beshbalik, enthroned Buyanshir, a descendant of the Yuan, as khan.

sentences.zh: 六年春，帝即以書諭本雅失裡曰：「自元運既訖，順帝后愛猷識理達臘至坤帖木兒凡六傳，瞬息之間，未聞一人善終者。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year, the emperor immediately sent a letter admonishing Buyanshir, saying: "Since the fortune of Yuan had ended, from Emperor Shun's consort Ayushiridara down to Kuntemür there were six successions; in the blink of an eye, not one is heard to have died a natural death."
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year the emperor wrote to Buyanshir: "Since the Yuan dynasty's fortune ran out, from Ayushiridara, consort of Emperor Shun, down to Kuntemür there have been six successions—and in that brief span not one is said to have died in his bed."

sentences.zh: 我皇考太祖高皇帝於元氏子孫，加意撫恤，來歸者輒令北還，如遣脫古思帖木兒歸，嗣為可汗，此南北人所共知。

translations.literal: "Our imperial father, the Taizu High Emperor, toward the descendants of the Yuan clan showed deliberate care and kindness; those who came to submit he always ordered to return north—as when he sent Toghus Temür back to succeed as khan. This is known to all north and south."
translations.idiomatic: "Our imperial father, the Hongwu Emperor, showed deliberate kindness to the Yuan imperial line: whenever one of them submitted, he sent him back north—as when he restored Toghus Temür as khan. North and south alike know this."

sentences.zh: 朕之心即皇考之心。

translations.literal: "My heart is my imperial father's heart."
translations.idiomatic: "My heart is my father's heart."

sentences.zh: 茲元氏宗祧不絕如線，去就之機，禍福由分，爾宜審處之。

translations.literal: "Now the Yuan ancestral line hangs by a thread; the moment of choosing between staying and leaving, and whether fortune or ruin follows, depends on your own judgment—you should consider this carefully."
translations.idiomatic: "Now the Yuan ancestral line hangs by a thread. Whether you stay or go, and whether fortune or ruin follows, is for you to decide—you must weigh it carefully."

sentences.zh: 」不聽。

translations.literal: He would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Buyanshir would not listen.

sentences.zh: 明年，獲其部曲完者帖木兒等二十二人，帝因復使給事中郭驥齎書往。

translations.literal: The next year they captured twenty-two of his followers including Wanzhetemür; the emperor therefore again sent the supervising secretary Guo Ji with a letter.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Ming captured twenty-two of his followers, including Wanzhetemür, and the emperor again dispatched Supervising Secretary Guo Ji with a letter.

sentences.zh: 驥被殺，帝怒。

translations.literal: Ji was killed; the emperor was enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ji was killed, and the emperor was enraged.

sentences.zh: 秋，命淇國公丘福為大將軍，武城侯王聰、同安侯火真副之，靖安侯王忠、安平侯李遠為左、右參將，將精騎十萬北討，諭以毋失機，毋輕犯敵，一舉未捷，俟再舉。

translations.literal: In autumn he ordered Qiu Fu, Duke of Qi, as great general, with Wang Cong, Marquis of Wucheng, and Huo Zhen, Marquis of Tong'an, as deputies, and Wang Zhong, Marquis of Jing'an, and Li Yuan, Marquis of Anping, as left and right staff generals, to lead one hundred thousand elite horsemen on a northern punitive campaign, instructing them not to miss the opportunity, not to lightly provoke the enemy, and if the first strike did not succeed, to wait for a second.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he appointed Qiu Fu, Duke of Qi, great general, with Wang Cong, Marquis of Wucheng, and Huo Zhen, Marquis of Tong'an, as deputies, and Wang Zhong, Marquis of Jing'an, and Li Yuan, Marquis of Anping, as left and right staff generals. With one hundred thousand elite horsemen they marched north to punish the Tartars, under strict orders not to miss their chance, not to provoke the enemy rashly, and if the first blow failed, to wait and strike again.

sentences.zh: 時本雅失裡已為瓦剌所襲破，與阿魯台徙居臚朐河。

translations.literal: At this time Buyanshir had already been attacked and broken by the Oirats and, with Arughtai, had moved to dwell on the Luqu River.
translations.idiomatic: By then Buyanshir had already been routed by the Oirats and, with Arughtai, had withdrawn to the Luqu River.

sentences.zh: 福率千騎先馳，遇游兵擊破之。

translations.literal: Fu led one thousand horsemen in a swift advance, encountered scouting troops, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Fu galloped ahead with one thousand horsemen, met enemy scouts, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 軍未集，福乘勝渡河追敵，敵輒佯敗引去。

translations.literal: The army had not yet assembled when Fu, exploiting the victory, crossed the river in pursuit; the enemy repeatedly feigned defeat and drew them on.
translations.idiomatic: Before the main army had assembled, Qiu Fu, emboldened by the victory, crossed the river in pursuit while the enemy repeatedly feigned defeat and drew him on.

sentences.zh: 諸將以帝命止福，福不聽。

translations.literal: The generals, citing the emperor's command, tried to stop Fu, but Fu would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The other generals, citing the emperor's orders, tried to stop him, but Qiu Fu would not listen.

sentences.zh: 敵眾奄至，圍之，五將軍皆沒。

translations.literal: The enemy host suddenly arrived and surrounded them; all five generals perished.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy host suddenly closed in and surrounded them; all five generals perished.

sentences.zh: 帝益怒。

translations.literal: The emperor was all the more enraged.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's rage only deepened.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝自將五十萬眾出塞。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor personally led five hundred thousand men out beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the emperor himself led five hundred thousand men beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 本雅失裡聞之懼，欲與阿魯台俱西，阿魯台不從，眾潰散，君臣始各為部。

translations.literal: When Buyanshir heard this he was afraid and wished to go west together with Arughtai; Arughtai would not follow, the host scattered, and ruler and minister at last each became a separate tribe.
translations.idiomatic: When Buyanshir heard this he was terrified and wished to flee west with Arughtai, but Arughtai refused to follow. Their forces broke apart, and at last ruler and minister each went his own way.

sentences.zh: 本雅失裡西奔，阿魯台東奔。

translations.literal: Buyanshir fled west; Arughtai fled east.
translations.idiomatic: Buyanshir fled west; Arughtai fled east.

sentences.zh: 帝追及斡難河，本雅失裡拒戰。

translations.literal: The emperor pursued to the Onon River; Buyanshir resisted in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pursued Buyanshir to the Onon River, where Buyanshir stood to fight.

sentences.zh: 帝麾兵奮擊，一呼敗之。

translations.literal: The emperor waved his troops to strike fiercely; with one shout they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor waved his troops forward in a fierce charge; at a single shout the enemy line broke.

sentences.zh: 本雅失裡棄輜重孳畜，以七騎遁。

translations.literal: Buyanshir abandoned baggage, livestock, and dependents and escaped with seven horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Buyanshir abandoned his baggage, livestock, and dependents and fled with only seven horsemen.

sentences.zh: 斡難河者，元太祖始興地也。

translations.literal: The Onon River—it was the place where the Yuan Founder first rose to power.
translations.idiomatic: The Onon River was where the Yuan founder had first begun his rise to power.

sentences.zh: 班師至靜虜鎮，遇阿魯台，帝使諭之降。

translations.literal: On the return march the army reached Jinglu Fortress, encountered Arughtai, and the emperor sent orders urging him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: As the army marched home and reached Jinglu Fortress, they encountered Arughtai, and the emperor sent word urging him to submit.

sentences.zh: 阿魯台欲來，眾不可，遂戰。

translations.literal: Arughtai wished to come, but the host would not allow it, and so they fought.
translations.idiomatic: Arughtai wished to surrender, but his followers refused, and battle was joined.

sentences.zh: 帝率精騎大呼衝擊，矢下如注，阿魯台墜馬，遂大敗，追奔百餘里乃還。

translations.literal: The emperor led elite cavalry in a great shouting charge; arrows fell like rain; Arughtai fell from his horse, and they were utterly defeated; they pursued the rout for more than a hundred li before returning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor led his elite cavalry in a thunderous charge. Arrows fell like rain, Arughtai was thrown from his horse, and his forces were utterly routed. The pursuit ran for more than a hundred li before the Ming troops turned back.

sentences.zh: 冬，阿魯台使來貢馬，帝納之。

translations.literal: In winter Arughtai's envoy came to offer tribute horses; the emperor accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Arughtai sent envoys bearing tribute horses, and the emperor accepted the tribute.

sentences.zh: 越二年，本雅失裡為瓦剌馬哈木等所殺。

translations.literal: Two years later Buyanshir was killed by the Oirats Mahamu and others.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Buyanshir was killed by Mahamu of the Oirats and his allies.

sentences.zh: 阿魯台已數入貢，帝俱厚報之，並還其向所俘同產兄妹二人。

translations.literal: Arughtai had already sent tribute several times; the emperor each time responded generously, and also returned two siblings of the same birth whom he had previously captured.
translations.idiomatic: Arughtai had already sent tribute on several occasions, and each time the emperor had rewarded him handsomely, returning as well two full siblings whom he had previously taken captive.

sentences.zh: 至是，奏馬哈木等弒其主，又擅立答裡巴，願輸誠內附，請為故主復仇。

translations.literal: At this time he memorialized that Mahamu and others had murdered their lord and arbitrarily installed Delbeg; he wished to offer sincerity and submit inwardly, and requested to avenge his former lord.
translations.idiomatic: Now he reported that Mahamu and the others had murdered their khan and installed Delbeg without authority. He pledged loyalty and offered to submit, asking permission to avenge his former lord.

sentences.zh: 天子義之，封為和寧王。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven approved his cause and enfeoffed him as Prince of Hening.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his cause, the emperor enfeoffed him as Prince of Hening.

sentences.zh: 自是，歲或一貢，或再貢，以為常。

translations.literal: From this time on, some years he sent tribute once, some years twice—this became the custom.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he sent tribute once or twice each year, and this became the established practice.

sentences.zh: 十二年，帝征瓦剌。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the emperor campaigned against the Oirats.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of the reign the emperor marched against the Oirats.

sentences.zh: 阿魯台使部長以下來朝會。

translations.literal: Arughtai sent tribal chiefs and subordinates to attend the court audience.
translations.idiomatic: Arughtai sent his tribal chiefs and their subordinates to attend an audience at court.

sentences.zh: 賜米五十石，乾肉、酒糗、彩幣有差。

translations.literal: They were granted fifty shi of grain, dried meat, wine and provisions, and colored silks in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: They were granted fifty shi of grain, together with dried meat, wine, provisions, and colored silks in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 十四年，以戰敗瓦剌，使來獻俘。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, because he had defeated the Oirats in battle, his envoys came to present captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, after defeating the Oirats in battle, he sent envoys to present captives to the court.

sentences.zh: 十九年，阿魯台貢使至邊，要劫行旅，帝諭使戒戢之，由是驕蹇不至。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, when Arughtai's tribute envoys reached the border they waylaid travelers; the emperor instructed the envoys to restrain them, whereupon they grew arrogant and ceased coming.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Arughtai's tribute envoys waylaid travelers at the border. The emperor sent word ordering them to cease, but they grew arrogant and stopped sending tribute altogether.

sentences.zh: 阿魯台之內附，困於瓦剌，窮蹙而南，思假息塞外。

translations.literal: Arughtai's submission inwardly came of being beset by the Oirats, driven to extremity and fleeing south, wishing to borrow rest beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Arughtai had submitted because he was hard pressed by the Oirats, driven to desperation and pushed south in hopes of finding refuge beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 帝納而封之，母妻皆為王太夫人、王夫人。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted him and enfeoffed him; his mother and wife were both made Grand Lady of the Prince and Lady of the Prince.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his submission and enfeoffed him; his mother and wife were both granted the titles Grand Lady of the Prince and Lady of the Prince.

sentences.zh: 數年生聚，畜牧日以蕃盛，遂慢我使者，拘留之。

translations.literal: Over several years they gathered and multiplied; livestock daily grew abundant, and then they slighted our envoys and detained them.
translations.idiomatic: Over the next several years his people recovered and multiplied, and their herds grew daily more abundant. Then he began to treat Ming envoys with contempt and detained them.

sentences.zh: 其貢使歸，多行劫掠，部落亦時來窺塞。

translations.literal: When his tribute envoys returned they often carried out robbery and plunder; his tribes also sometimes came to spy on the frontier passes.
translations.idiomatic: On the return journey his tribute envoys frequently robbed travelers, and his tribesmen also periodically prowled the frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 二十年春，大人興和。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twentieth year he launched a major attack on Xinghe.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twentieth year he launched a major assault on Xinghe.

sentences.zh: 於是詔親征之。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued ordering a personal campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon ordered a personal expedition against him.

sentences.zh: 阿魯台聞大軍出，懼，其母妻皆詈之曰：「大明皇帝何負爾，而必為逆！

translations.literal: When Arughtai heard that the great army was marching out he was afraid; his mother and wife all cursed him, saying, "What has the Great Ming emperor done to wrong you, that you must persist in rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: When Arughtai learned that the great army was on the march he was terrified. His mother and wife cursed him, saying, "What has the Great Ming emperor done to wrong you, that you must persist in rebellion!

sentences.zh: 」於是盡棄其輜重馬畜於闊灤海側，以其孥直北徙。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he abandoned all his baggage and livestock beside Lake Kuoluan and moved his dependents due north.
translations.idiomatic: " He then abandoned all his baggage and livestock beside Lake Kuoluan and fled north with his dependents.

sentences.zh: 帝命焚其輜重，收其馬畜，遂班師。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered his baggage burned and his livestock seized, and then the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the abandoned baggage burned and the livestock seized, then marched the army home.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，邊將言阿魯台將入寇。

translations.literal: The next autumn the frontier generals reported that Arughtai was about to invade.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn frontier commanders reported that Arughtai was preparing to raid the border.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「彼意朕必不復出，當先駐塞下待之。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "He thinks that I will surely not come out again; I should first encamp below the passes and wait for him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "He thinks I will never campaign beyond the frontier again. I shall encamp below the passes and wait for him.

sentences.zh: 」遂部分寧陽侯陳懋為先鋒，至宿嵬山不見敵，遇王子也先土干率妻子部屬來降。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he deployed Ningyang Marquis Chen Mao as vanguard; when they reached Mount Suwei no enemy was seen, but they encountered the prince Esen Toghan leading his wife, children, and followers to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: " He then deployed Ningyang Marquis Chen Mao as vanguard. When the vanguard reached Mount Suwei no enemy was found, but they encountered the prince Esen Toghan, who came to surrender with his wife, children, and followers.

sentences.zh: 帝封為忠勇王，賜姓名曰金忠。

translations.literal: The emperor enfeoffed him as Prince of Zhongyong and granted him the surname and personal name Jin Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor enfeoffed him as Prince of Zhongyong and granted him the Chinese name Jin Zhong.

sentences.zh: 忠勇王至京師，數請擊敵自效。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Zhongyong reached the capital he repeatedly requested to strike the enemy and prove his worth.
translations.idiomatic: After reaching the capital, the Prince of Zhongyong repeatedly asked to lead troops against the enemy and prove his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「姑待之。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "For the present, wait.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Let us wait for now.

sentences.zh: 」二十二年春，開平守將奏阿魯台盜邊，群臣勸帝如忠勇王言。

translations.literal: " In the spring of the twenty-second year the garrison commander at Kaiping memorialized that Arughtai was raiding the border; the ministers urged the emperor to follow the Prince of Zhongyong's advice.
translations.idiomatic: " In the spring of the twenty-second year the Kaiping garrison commander reported that Arughtai was raiding the frontier, and the ministers urged the emperor to take the Prince of Zhongyong's advice.

sentences.zh: 帝復親征，師次荅蘭納木兒河，得諜者，知阿魯台遠遁。

translations.literal: The emperor again led a personal campaign; the army halted at the Tula River, obtained a spy, and learned that Arughtai had fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again took the field in person. When the army halted at the Tula River, a spy revealed that Arughtai had already fled deep into the steppe.

sentences.zh: 帝意亦厭兵，乃下詔暴阿魯台罪惡，而宥其所部來降者，止勿殺。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind also wearied of war; he thereupon issued an edict exposing Arughtai's crimes, yet pardoning those of his followers who came to surrender, ordering that they be spared and not killed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had grown weary of campaigning. He issued an edict denouncing Arughtai's crimes but pardoning those of his followers who surrendered, ordering that they be spared.

sentences.zh: 車駕還，崩於榆木川。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage returned, and the emperor died at Yumu River.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned homeward but died on the Yumu River before reaching the capital.

sentences.zh: 未幾，阿魯台使來貢馬，仁宗已登極，詔納之。

translations.literal: Before long Arughtai's envoy came to offer tribute horses; the Renzong Emperor had already ascended the throne, and an edict was issued accepting the tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Arughtai sent envoys bearing tribute horses. The Renzong Emperor had already taken the throne, and he ordered the tribute accepted.

sentences.zh: 自是，歲修職貢如永樂時。

translations.literal: From this time on, tribute was sent each year as in the Yongle era.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter tribute was sent each year as it had been during the Yongle reign.

sentences.zh: 時阿魯台數敗於瓦剌，部曲離散。

translations.literal: At this time Arughtai had repeatedly been defeated by the Oirats, and his followers had scattered.
translations.idiomatic: By then Arughtai had suffered repeated defeats at the hands of the Oirats, and his followers had scattered.

sentences.zh: 其屬把的等先後來歸，朝廷皆予官職，賜鈔幣，詔有司給供具。

translations.literal: His followers Badi and others came to submit in succession; the court all granted them official posts, bestowed paper money and silks, and ordered the relevant offices to provide supplies.
translations.idiomatic: His followers, including Badi, submitted one after another. The court granted them official posts, bestowed paper money and silks, and ordered the appropriate offices to provide for their needs.

sentences.zh: 自後來歸者，悉如例。

translations.literal: Those who came to submit afterward were all treated according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: All who submitted thereafter were treated according to the same precedent.

sentences.zh: 阿魯台日益蹙，乃率其屬東走兀良哈，駐牧遼塞。

translations.literal: Arughtai grew daily more pressed; he then led his followers east to the Uriangkhai and encamped to pasture on the Liao frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Arughtai's position grew daily more desperate. He led his followers east to the Uriangkhai and encamped to pasture along the Liao frontier.

sentences.zh: 諸將請出兵掩擊之，帝不聽。

translations.literal: The generals requested to send troops to strike him by surprise; the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The generals asked permission to launch a surprise attack, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 宣德九年，阿魯台復為脫脫不花所襲，妻子死，孳畜略盡，獨與其子失捏乾等徙居母納山、察罕腦剌等處。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Xuande, Arughtai was again attacked by Togto Buqa; his wife and children died, livestock and dependents were nearly all lost, and he alone moved with his son Shinigin and others to dwell at Mount Mona, Chaghan Nao'er, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Xuande, Arughtai was again attacked by Togto Buqa. His wife and children were killed, his livestock and dependents were nearly all lost, and he fled with only his son Shinigin and a few others to Mount Mona, Chaghan Nao'er, and other refuges.

sentences.zh: 未幾，瓦剌脫懽襲殺阿魯台及失捏干，於是阿魯檯子阿卜只俺及其孫妻速木答思等喪敗無依，來乞內附。

translations.literal: Before long the Oirat Toghan attacked and killed Arughtai and Shinigin; thereupon Arughtai's son Abuzhan and his grandson's wife Sumudasi and others, bereft and without support after their defeat, came begging to submit inwardly.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Oirat leader Toghan attacked and killed Arughtai and Shinigin. Arughtai's son Abuzhan, his grandson's wife Sumudasi, and others, left destitute after their defeat, came begging to submit to the Ming.

sentences.zh: 帝憐而撫之。

translations.literal: The emperor took pity on them and comforted them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took pity on them and extended his protection.

sentences.zh: 未幾，脫脫不花捕阿台等殺之。

translations.literal: Before long Togto Buqa captured Atai and others and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Togto Buqa captured Atai and his followers and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 脫脫不花者，故元後，韃靼長也。

translations.literal: Togto Buqa was a descendant of the former Yuan and a Tartar chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: Togto Buqa was a descendant of the Yuan imperial house and a chieftain of the Tartars.

sentences.zh: 瓦剌脫忄雚既擊殺阿魯台，悉收其部，兼併賢義、安樂二王之眾，欲自立為可汗。

translations.literal: After the Oirat Toghan had attacked and killed Arughtai, he gathered in all his tribes, annexed the followers of the Princes of Xianyi and Anle, and wished to install himself as khan.
translations.idiomatic: After the Oirat leader Toghan had killed Arughtai, he absorbed all of Arughtai's tribes and annexed the forces of the Princes of Xianyi and Anle, intending to proclaim himself khan.

sentences.zh: 眾不可，乃立脫脫不花，以阿魯台眾屬之，自為丞相，陽推奉之，實不承其號令。

translations.literal: The host would not allow it; he then installed Togto Buqa, assigned Arughtai's followers to him, and made himself chief minister, outwardly deferring to him while in fact not obeying his commands.
translations.idiomatic: His followers would not accept this, so he installed Togto Buqa as khan, assigned Arughtai's followers to him, and took the title of chief minister himself—paying lip service to Togto Buqa while ignoring his orders in practice.

sentences.zh: 脫懽死，子也先嗣，益桀驁自雄，諸部皆下之，脫脫不花具可汗名而已。

translations.literal: When Toghan died his son Esen succeeded him, grew ever more fierce and proud, and all the tribes submitted to him; Togto Buqa possessed only the name of khan.
translations.idiomatic: When Toghan died his son Esen succeeded him. Esen grew ever more fierce and overbearing until all the tribes submitted to him, leaving Togto Buqa with nothing but the empty title of khan.

sentences.zh: 脫脫不花歲來朝貢，天子皆厚報之，比諸蕃有加，書稱之曰達達可汗，賜賚並及其妃。

translations.literal: Togto Buqa came each year to court with tribute; the Son of Heaven each time responded generously, treating him more favorably than other foreign states, addressing him in writing as the Dada Khan, and bestowing gifts on him and his consort alike.
translations.idiomatic: Togto Buqa sent tribute to court each year, and the emperor always responded with lavish gifts, treating him more generously than other foreign rulers. Imperial letters addressed him as the Dada Khan, and gifts were bestowed on him and his consort alike.

sentences.zh: 十四年秋，也先謀大舉入寇，脫脫不花止之曰：「吾儕服食，多資大明，何忍為此？

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourteenth year Esen plotted a major invasion; Togto Buqa stopped him, saying, "Our clothing and food depend largely on the Great Ming—how can we bear to do this?
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fourteenth year Esen planned a major invasion. Togto Buqa tried to stop him, saying, "Our clothing and food depend largely on the Great Ming—how can we bring ourselves to do this?

sentences.zh: 」也先不聽，曰：「可汗不為，吾當自為。

translations.literal: " Esen would not listen and said, "If the khan will not do it, I shall do it myself.
translations.idiomatic: " Esen refused to listen. "If the khan will not act," he said, "I shall act on my own.

sentences.zh: 」遂分道，俾脫脫不花侵遼東，而自擁眾從大同入。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they divided their forces, ordering Togto Buqa to raid Liaodong while he himself led his host in through Datong.
translations.idiomatic: " They then divided their forces, sending Togto Buqa to raid Liaodong while Esen himself led his army in through Datong.

sentences.zh: 帝親征之，駕於土木陷焉。

translations.literal: The emperor personally campaigned against them, and the imperial carriage was trapped at Tumu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marched out to meet them in person, and the imperial army was trapped at Tumu.

sentences.zh: 景皇帝自監國即位，尊帝為太上皇帝。

translations.literal: The Jing Emperor ascended the throne from his regency and honored the former emperor as the Retired Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The Jing Emperor, who had been regent, took the throne and honored the captured emperor as the Retired Emperor.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，上皇歸自也先所。

translations.literal: The next autumn the Retired Emperor returned from Esen's custody.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn the Retired Emperor returned from captivity in Esen's camp.

sentences.zh: 事載《瓦剌傳》。

translations.literal: The affair is recorded in the "Biography of the Oirats."
translations.idiomatic: The full account is given in the Biography of the Oirats.

sentences.zh: 脫脫不花自上皇歸後，修貢益勤。

translations.literal: After the Retired Emperor's return Togto Buqa sent tribute with ever greater diligence.
translations.idiomatic: After the Retired Emperor's return Togto Buqa sent tribute with ever greater diligence.

sentences.zh: 嘗妻也先姊，生子，也先欲立之，不從。

translations.literal: He had once taken Esen's elder sister as wife and had a son by her; Esen wished to install the boy as khan, but Togto Buqa would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: He had married Esen's elder sister and had a son by her. Esen wished to install the boy as khan, but Togto Buqa refused.

sentences.zh: 也先亦疑其與中國通，將害己，遂治兵相攻。

translations.literal: Esen also suspected that he was in communication with China and would harm him, and so he marshaled troops to attack one another.
translations.idiomatic: Esen also suspected that Togto Buqa was colluding with China and plotting against him, and so he mobilized his forces for war.

sentences.zh: 也先殺脫脫不花，收其妻子孳畜，給諸部屬，而自立為可汗。

translations.literal: Esen killed Togto Buqa, seized his wife, children, and livestock, distributed them among the tribal followers, and installed himself as khan.
translations.idiomatic: Esen killed Togto Buqa, seized his wife, children, and livestock, distributed the spoils among his followers, and proclaimed himself khan.

sentences.zh: 時景皇帝二年也。

translations.literal: This was in the second year of the Jing Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the second year of the Jing Emperor's reign.

sentences.zh: 朝廷稱也先為瓦剌可汗。

translations.literal: The court addressed Esen as Khan of the Oirats.
translations.idiomatic: The court addressed Esen as Khan of the Oirats.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為所部阿剌知院所殺。

translations.literal: Before long he was killed by Alzhiyuan of his own following.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was killed by Alzhiyuan, one of his own followers.

sentences.zh: 韃靼部長孛來復攻破阿剌，求脫脫不花子麻兒可兒立之，號小王子。

translations.literal: The Tartar chieftain Bolai again defeated Alzhiyuan, sought out Togto Buqa's son Markörgis and installed him, styling him the Little Prince.
translations.idiomatic: The Tartar chieftain Bolai defeated Alzhiyuan in turn, found Togto Buqa's son Markörgis, and installed him under the title Little Prince.

sentences.zh: 阿剌死，而孛來與其屬毛裡孩等皆雄視部中，於是韃靼復熾。

translations.literal: Alzhiyuan died, and Bolai together with his follower Molihai and others all dominated the tribes; thus the Tartars again flourished.
translations.idiomatic: After Alzhiyuan's death Bolai and his follower Molihai dominated the tribes, and Tartar power revived.

sentences.zh: 景泰六年遣使入貢。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jingtai envoys were sent to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Jingtai they sent envoys to offer tribute.

sentences.zh: 英宗復辟，遣都督馬政往賜故伯顏帖木兒妻幣。

translations.literal: When the Yingzong Emperor restored the throne he dispatched Commissioner-in-Chief Ma Zheng to bestow silks on the widow of the late Bayan Temür.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yingzong Emperor regained the throne he sent Commissioner-in-Chief Ma Zheng to bestow silks on the widow of the late Bayan Temür.

sentences.zh: 孛來留之，而遣使入賀，欲獻璽。

translations.literal: Bolai detained him, but sent envoys to offer congratulations and wished to present the imperial seal.
translations.idiomatic: Bolai detained Ma Zheng but sent his own envoys to offer congratulations and proposed to present the imperial seal.

sentences.zh: 帝敕之曰：「璽已非真，即真，亦秦不祥物耳，獻否從爾便。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed them, saying, "The seal is already not genuine; even if it were genuine, it is also the ill-omened object of Qin—whether you present it or not is for you to decide.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "The seal is already a forgery; even if it were genuine, it would still be the ill-omened seal of Qin. Present it or not, as you please.

sentences.zh: 第無留我使，以速爾禍。

translations.literal: Only do not detain my envoy, lest you hasten your own ruin.
translations.idiomatic: But do not detain my envoy, or you will only hasten your own ruin.

sentences.zh: 」時敵數寇威遠諸衛，夏，定遠伯石彪敗之於磨兒山。

translations.literal: " At this time the enemy repeatedly raided the guards around Weiyuan; in summer Dingyuan Earl Shi Biao defeated them at Mount Mo'er.
translations.idiomatic: " Meanwhile the enemy repeatedly raided the guards around Weiyuan. That summer Dingyuan Earl Shi Biao defeated them at Mount Mo'er.

sentences.zh: 天順二年，孛來大舉寇陝西，安遠侯柳溥御之輒敗，而飾小捷以聞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianshun Bolai launched a major raid into Shaanxi; Anyuan Marquis Liu Pu met him and was repeatedly defeated, yet reported minor victories.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianshun Bolai launched a major raid into Shaanxi. Anyuan Marquis Liu Pu met him and was repeatedly defeated, yet reported minor victories to the court.

sentences.zh: 明年春，敵入安邊營，石彪等破之，都督周賢、指揮李钅監戰死。

translations.literal: The next spring the enemy entered Anbian Camp; Shi Biao and others defeated them, but Commissioner-in-Chief Zhou Xian and Commander Li Jian died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring the enemy entered Anbian Camp. Shi Biao and others routed them, but Commissioner-in-Chief Zhou Xian and Commander Li Jian were killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 四年復寇榆林，彰武伯楊信拒卻之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year they again raided Yulin; Zhangwu Earl Yang Xin repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year they raided Yulin again, but Zhangwu Earl Yang Xin drove them back.

sentences.zh: 再入，敗之於金雞峪。

translations.literal: When they entered again he defeated them at Jinjiyu.
translations.idiomatic: When they invaded again he defeated them at Jinjiyu.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復大掠陝西諸邊，廷臣請治各守將罪，帝宥之。

translations.literal: Before long they again carried out major plunder along the Shaanxi frontier; court officials requested that the frontier commanders be punished, but the emperor pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they raided widely along the Shaanxi frontier again. Court officials asked that the frontier commanders be punished, but the emperor pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 五年春，寇入平虜城，誘指揮許顒等入伏，殺之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year the raiders entered Pinglu Fortress, lured Commanders Xu Yong and others into an ambush, and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year the raiders entered Pinglu Fortress, lured Commanders Xu Yong and others into an ambush, and killed them.

sentences.zh: 邊報日亟，命侍郎白圭、都御史王竑往視師。

translations.literal: Frontier reports grew daily more urgent; Vice Minister Bai Gui and Censor-in-Chief Wang Hong were ordered to go inspect the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier reports grew daily more urgent, and Vice Minister Bai Gui and Censor-in-Chief Wang Hong were dispatched to inspect the armies.

sentences.zh: 秋，孛來求款，帝使詹升齎敕往諭。

translations.literal: In autumn Bolai sought peace; the emperor sent Zhan Sheng bearing an edict to instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Bolai sought peace, and the emperor sent Zhan Sheng with an edict to address him.

sentences.zh: 孛來遣使隨升來貢，請改大同舊貢道，而由陝西蘭縣入，許之。

translations.literal: Bolai sent envoys to follow Sheng and offer tribute, requesting to change from the old tribute route through Datong and enter instead by Lan County in Shaanxi; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Bolai sent envoys to accompany Sheng and offer tribute, asking to abandon the old tribute route through Datong and enter instead by Lan County in Shaanxi. The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復糾其屬毛裡孩等入河西。

translations.literal: Before long he again gathered his follower Molihai and others to enter Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he again rallied his follower Molihai and others to raid Hexi.

sentences.zh: 明年春，圭等分巡西邊，圭遇敵於固原川，竑遇敵於紅崖子川，皆破之。

translations.literal: The next spring Gui and the others made separate tours of the western frontier; Gui encountered the enemy at Guyuan River and Wang Hong at Hongyazi River, and both defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring Gui and the others toured the western frontier separately. Gui defeated the enemy at Guyuan River, and Wang Hong defeated them at Hongyazi River.

sentences.zh: 帝賜璽書獎勵，敕孛來使臣仍從大同入貢。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed sealed letters of commendation and ordered Bolai's envoys to resume entering with tribute through Datong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent sealed letters of commendation and ordered Bolai's envoys to resume the tribute route through Datong.

sentences.zh: 時麻兒可兒復與孛來相仇殺。

translations.literal: At this time Markörgis again feuded and fought with Bolai.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Markörgis was again locked in mutual raids and killings with Bolai.

sentences.zh: 麻兒可兒死，眾共立馬可古兒吉思，亦號小王子。

translations.literal: When Markörgis died the host jointly installed Mongke Gerisen, also styled the Little Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Markörgis died the tribes jointly installed Mongke Gerisen, who was also styled the Little Prince.

sentences.zh: 自是，韃靼部長益各專擅。

translations.literal: From this time on, Tartar chieftains increasingly each acted on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: From this time on Tartar chieftains increasingly ruled their own domains independently.

sentences.zh: 小王子稀通中國，傳世次，多莫可考。

translations.literal: The Little Prince rarely communicated with China; the line of succession is for the most part beyond verification.
translations.idiomatic: The Little Prince had little contact with China, and the line of succession is largely impossible to trace.

sentences.zh: 孛來等每歲入貢，數寇掠，往來塞下，以西攻瓦剌為辭，又數要劫三衛。

translations.literal: Bolai and others sent tribute each year yet repeatedly raided and plundered, moving back and forth below the passes; they used raids westward against the Oirats as a pretext, and repeatedly waylaid the Three Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Bolai and others sent tribute each year yet repeatedly raided the frontier, moving back and forth below the passes. They claimed to be campaigning west against the Oirats, but also repeatedly waylaid the Three Guards.

sentences.zh: 七年冬，貢使及關，帝卻之，以大學士李賢言乃止。

translations.literal: In the winter of the seventh year, when tribute envoys reached the pass the emperor rejected them, but stopped only upon Grand Secretary Li Xian's advice.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the seventh year the emperor rejected Bolai's tribute envoys at the pass, but relented only after Grand Secretary Li Xian intervened.

sentences.zh: 八年春，御史陳選言：「韃靼部落，孛來最強，又密招三衛諸蕃，相結屯住。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year Censor Chen Xuan memorialized, saying, "Among the Tartar tribes Bolai is strongest; he has also secretly summoned the various peoples of the Three Guards to join him and encamp together.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighth year Censor Chen Xuan memorialized: "Among the Tartar tribes Bolai is the strongest. He has also secretly summoned the peoples of the Three Guards to join him and encamp together.

sentences.zh: 去冬來朝，要我賞宴，窺我虛實，其犯邊之情已露。

translations.literal: Last winter he came to court, demanded rewards and banquets from us, and spied on our strengths and weaknesses; his intent to violate the border has already been exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Last winter he came to court, demanded rewards and banquets, and spied on our defenses. His intent to raid the frontier is already plain.

sentences.zh: 而我邊關守臣，因循怠慢，城堡不修，甲仗不利，軍士不操習，甚至富者納月錢而安閒，貧者迫飢寒而逃竄。

translations.literal: Yet our frontier commanders are complacent and negligent: fortresses are not repaired, armor and weapons are not serviceable, soldiers are not drilled—even the wealthy pay monthly fees to live at ease, while the poor, driven by hunger and cold, flee and scatter.
translations.idiomatic: Yet our frontier commanders are complacent and negligent. Fortresses go unrepaired, arms and armor are unserviceable, and soldiers receive no drill. The wealthy pay monthly fees to avoid duty, while the poor, driven by hunger and cold, desert and flee.

sentences.zh: 邊備廢弛，緩急何恃？

translations.literal: Frontier defenses are in decay—on what shall we rely in an emergency?
translations.idiomatic: Frontier defenses lie in ruins—what shall we rely on in an emergency?

sentences.zh: 乞敕在邊諸臣，痛革前弊。

translations.literal: I beg that frontier officials be ordered to thoroughly reform past abuses.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that frontier officials be ordered to root out these abuses.

sentences.zh: 其鎮守、備御等官，亦宜以時黜陟，庶能者知奮，怠者知警。

translations.literal: The garrison, defense, and other officials should also be promoted or demoted in timely fashion, so that the capable may know to strive and the negligent may know to take warning.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison and defense officials should also be promoted or dismissed in timely fashion, so that the capable are encouraged to strive and the negligent are put on notice.

sentences.zh: 至厄塞要害之處，或益官軍，或設營堡，或用墩台，咸須處置得宜，歲遣大臣巡視，庶邊防有備，寇氛可戢。

translations.literal: As for strategic passes and key points, whether by adding garrison troops, establishing camps and fortresses, or using beacon towers—all must be disposed appropriately; each year grand ministers should be dispatched to inspect, so that frontier defenses may be prepared and raiders restrained.
translations.idiomatic: At strategic passes and key points, whether by adding garrison troops, building camps and fortresses, or erecting beacon towers, all measures must be properly arranged. Each year senior officials should be sent to inspect the frontier, so that defenses may be ready and raiders restrained.

sentences.zh: 」報聞。

translations.literal: " The memorial was noted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was noted.

sentences.zh: 成化元年春，孛來誘兀良哈九萬騎入遼河，武安侯鄭宏御卻之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Chenghua Bolai lured ninety thousand Uriangkhai horsemen into the Liao River; Wu'an Marquis Zheng Hong met and repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first year of Chenghua Bolai lured ninety thousand Uriangkhai horsemen into the Liao River valley. Wu'an Marquis Zheng Hong met and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 秋，散掠延綏。

translations.literal: In autumn they scattered in raids across Yan-Sui.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn they scattered in raids across Yan-Sui.

sentences.zh: 冬，復大入。

translations.literal: In winter they again launched a major raid.
translations.idiomatic: That winter they launched another major raid.

sentences.zh: 命彰武伯楊信率山西兵，都御史項忠率陝西兵御之，少卻。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Zhangwu Earl Yang Xin to lead Shanxi troops and Censor-in-Chief Xiang Zhong to lead Shaanxi troops to meet them; the enemy withdrew slightly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Zhangwu Earl Yang Xin to lead Shanxi troops and Censor-in-Chief Xiang Zhong to lead Shaanxi troops against them, and the raiders fell back somewhat.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復渡河曲，圍黃甫川堡，官軍力戰，乃引去。

translations.literal: Before long they again crossed the river bend, besieged Huangfuchuan Fortress, and withdrew only after government troops fought fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they crossed the river bend again, besieged Huangfuchuan Fortress, and withdrew only after government troops fought them off.

sentences.zh: 始，韃靼之來也，或在遼東、宣府、大同，或在寧夏、莊浪、甘肅，去來無常，為患不久。

translations.literal: At first, when the Tartars came they might appear in Liaodong, Xuanfu, or Datong, or in Ningxia, Zhuanglang, or Gansu; their comings and goings were irregular and the harm did not last long.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Tartars might strike Liaodong, Xuanfu, or Datong, or Ningxia, Zhuanglang, or Gansu; their movements were erratic and the damage seldom lasted.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，始犯延慶，然部落少，不敢深入。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingtai reign they first violated Yanqing, but their tribes were few and they did not dare penetrate deeply.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Jingtai years they first raided Yanqing, but their bands were small and they did not dare push far inland.

sentences.zh: 天順間，有阿羅出者，率屬潛入河套居之，遂逼近西邊。

translations.literal: During the Tianshun period there was one Aluochu, who led his followers secretly into the Ordos bend to dwell there, and thus drew near the western frontier.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianshun period a leader named Aluochu led his followers secretly into the Ordos bend to settle there, pressing close against the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 河套，古朔方郡，唐張仁願築三受降城處也。

translations.literal: The Ordos bend was the ancient Shuofang commandery, the place where Tang Zhang Renyuan built the three cities that received surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Ordos bend was the ancient Shuofang commandery, where the Tang general Zhang Renyuan had built the three cities that received surrender.

sentences.zh: 地在黃河南，自寧夏至偏頭關，延袤二千里，饒水草，外為東勝衛。

translations.literal: The land lay south of the Yellow River, from Ningxia to Piantou Pass, stretching two thousand li; it was rich in grass and water, and beyond it lay the guard of Dongsheng.
translations.idiomatic: It lay south of the Yellow River, from Ningxia to Piantou Pass—a stretch of two thousand li rich in pasture and water—with the guard of Dongsheng beyond.

sentences.zh: 東勝而外，土平衍，敵來，一騎不能隱，明初守之，後以曠絕內徙。

translations.literal: Beyond Dongsheng the ground was level and open; when the enemy came not a single horseman could hide. In the early Ming it was garrisoned, but later, because the region was remote and desolate, the garrisons were withdrawn inward.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond Dongsheng the land was flat and open, offering no cover even for a lone rider. The early Ming had garrisoned it, but later, finding the region too remote, the court withdrew the posts inland.

sentences.zh: 至是，孛來與小王子、毛裡孩等先後繼至，擄中國人為鄉導，抄掠延綏無虛時，而邊事以棘。

translations.literal: By this time Bolai, the Little Prince, Molihai, and others arrived in succession; they seized Chinese as guides and raided Yan-Sui without respite, and frontier affairs grew critical.
translations.idiomatic: By then Bolai, the Little Prince, Molihai, and others had arrived in turn. They took Chinese captives as guides and raided Yan-Sui without pause, and the frontier crisis sharpened.

sentences.zh: 二年夏，大入延綏。

translations.literal: In the summer of the second year they launched a major raid into Yan-Sui.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, summer, they launched a major raid into Yan-Sui.

sentences.zh: 帝命楊信充總兵官，都督趙勝為副，率京軍及諸邊卒二萬人討之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Yang Xin to serve as supreme commander, with Regional Commander Zhao Sheng as his deputy, to lead twenty thousand capital troops and frontier soldiers against them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Yang Xin supreme commander, with Regional Commander Zhao Sheng as his deputy, and ordered them to lead twenty thousand capital troops and frontier soldiers against the raiders.

sentences.zh: 信先以議事赴闕，未至。

translations.literal: Xin had first gone to court to discuss affairs and had not yet arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xin had gone to court first to consult on strategy and had not yet reached the frontier.

sentences.zh: 敵散掠平涼，入靈州及固原，長驅寇靜寧、隆德諸處。

translations.literal: The enemy scattered in raids across Pingliang, entered Lingzhou and Guyuan, and drove deep to plunder Jingning, Longde, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders scattered across Pingliang, entered Lingzhou and Guyuan, and swept deep into Jingning, Longde, and neighboring districts.

sentences.zh: 冬，復入延綏，參將湯胤績戰死。

translations.literal: In winter they again entered Yan-Sui; Assistant Commander Tang Yinji died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: That winter they entered Yan-Sui again, and Assistant Commander Tang Yinji was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 未幾，諸部內爭，孛來弒馬可古兒吉思，毛裡孩殺孛來，更立他可汗。

translations.literal: Before long the tribes fell to internal strife: Bolai murdered Mongke Gerisen, Molihai killed Bolai, and they installed another khan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the tribes turned on one another. Bolai murdered Mongke Gerisen; Molihai killed Bolai in turn and installed another khan.

sentences.zh: 斡羅出者復與毛裡孩相仇殺，毛裡孩遂殺其所立可汗，逐斡羅出，而遣使入貢。

translations.literal: Wolochu again feuded and fought with Molihai; Molihai then killed the khan he had installed, expelled Wolochu, and sent envoys to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Wolochu again clashed with Molihai. Molihai killed the khan he had installed, drove Wolochu out, and sent envoys to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 尋渡河掠大同。

translations.literal: Soon afterward they crossed the river and raided Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward they crossed the river and raided Datong.

sentences.zh: 三年春，帝命撫寧侯硃永等征之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year the emperor ordered Funing Marquis Zhu Yong and others to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year the emperor ordered Funing Marquis Zhu Yong and others to take the field against them.
