translations.idiomatic: Bushitu has fled west into the Ordos loop. Baitai Taiji escaped only by his own exertions. Harachan's followers have been largely captured and are of little use.

sentences.zh: 永邵卜最強，約三十萬人，合卜失兔所部並聯絡朵顏三十六家及哈喇嗔餘眾，可以御插漢。

translations.literal: Yong Shaobu is strongest, about three hundred thousand people; together with Bushitu's division and also linking the thirty-six households of Duoyan and Harachan's remaining followers, they can resist Cha Han.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Shaobu is the strongest, with some three hundred thousand followers. Together with Bushitu's tribes, allied to the thirty-six Duoyan clans and Harachan's survivors, they could hold Cha Han at bay.

sentences.zh: 然與其構之，水如撫而用之。

translations.literal: Yet rather than setting them at odds, it is not as good as pacifying and employing them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet rather than pit them against each other, it would be better to win them over and put them to use.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「插漢意不受撫，奈何？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Cha Han's intention is not to accept pacification—what then?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Cha Han has no intention of accepting pacification. What then?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「當從容籠絡。

translations.literal: " He replied saying: "One should gradually and at ease win them over.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "We should win them over patiently, by degrees.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「如不款何？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "If they do not submit, what then?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor asked, "And if they refuse to submit?

sentences.zh: 」象乾復密奏，帝善之，命往與督師袁崇煥共計。

translations.literal: " Xiangqian again submitted a secret memorial; the emperor approved it and ordered him to go and jointly plan with supreme commander Yuan Chonghuan.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiangqian then submitted a secret memorial. The emperor approved and ordered him to go consult with supreme commander Yuan Chonghuan.

sentences.zh: 象乾至邊，與崇煥議合，皆言西靖而東自寧，虎不款，而東西並急，因定歲予插金八萬一千兩，以示羈縻。

translations.literal: Xiangqian reached the frontier and deliberated with Chonghuan; both said that if the west is pacified the east will be quiet of itself; the Tiger would not submit, yet east and west were both urgent; they therefore fixed annual granting to the Cha of eighty-one thousand taels of gold to show restraint and control.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangqian reached the frontier and met with Chonghuan. Both agreed that pacifying the west would quiet the east—but with Hudun Tu refusing to submit and pressure mounting on both fronts, they settled on an annual payment of eighty-one thousand taels to the Cha Han to keep him in check.

sentences.zh: 大同巡撫張宗衡上言：「插來宣大，駐新城，去大同僅二百里，三閱月未敢近前，飢餓窮乏，插與我等耳。

translations.literal: Datong grand coordinator Zhang Zongheng submitted saying: "The Cha came to Xuan-Datong and encamped at New City, only two hundred li from Datong; three months passed and they dared not advance—hunger, exhaustion, and destitution; the Cha and we are the same.
translations.idiomatic: Datong grand coordinator Zhang Zongheng wrote: "The Cha Han came to Xuan-Datong and encamped at New City, only two hundred li from Datong. Three months have passed and they still dare not advance—they are starving and destitute. They are no stronger than we are.

sentences.zh: 插恃撫金為命，兩年不得，資用已竭，食盡馬乏，暴骨成莽。

translations.literal: The Cha relies on pacification gold for their life; two years without receiving it, supplies and expenses are exhausted, food gone and horses depleted, exposed bones forming wilderness.
translations.idiomatic: The Cha Han lives on pacification payments. Two years without receiving them have exhausted their resources. Their food is gone, their horses spent, and bleached bones litter the wilderness.

sentences.zh: 插之望款不啻望歲，而我遺之金繒、牛羊、茶果、米谷無算，是我適中其欲也。

translations.literal: The Cha's hope for submission is no less than hope for a harvest year, yet we send them gold silks, cattle and sheep, tea and fruit, rice and grain beyond measure—this is we precisely hitting their desire.
translations.idiomatic: The Cha Han's longing to submit is as desperate as a farmer's prayer for rain, yet we have sent them endless gold, silk, cattle, sheep, tea, fruit, rice, and grain—playing straight into their hands.

sentences.zh: 插炰烋悖慢，耳目不忍睹聞，方急款尚如是。

translations.literal: The Cha is ferocious, violent, perverse and insolent—eyes and ears cannot bear to see or hear; even while urgently seeking submission they are still like this.
translations.idiomatic: The Cha Han is savage, arrogant, and insolent beyond what eyes can witness or ears endure—yet even as he begs to submit he behaves this way.

sentences.zh: 使插士馬豐飽，其憑陵狂逞，可勝道哉。

translations.literal: If the Cha's soldiers and horses are well fed and full, their relying on strength for reckless violence—can it be told in full?
translations.idiomatic: If we feed and arm the Cha Han's forces, how much worse will his predatory rampages become?

sentences.zh: 」象乾言：「款局垂成而復棼之，既示插以不信，亦非所以為國謀。

translations.literal: " Xiangqian said: "The submission arrangement was nearly complete yet is tangled again; this both shows the Cha distrust and is also not the way to plan for the state.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiangqian replied: "The pacification is nearly settled. To unravel it now would show the Cha Han we cannot be trusted—and that is no way to serve the state.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，帝是象乾議，詔宗衡毋得異同。

translations.literal: " When the memorial entered, the emperor approved Xiangqian's deliberation and edicted that Zongheng must not dissent.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial arrived the emperor sided with Xiangqian and ordered Zongheng to offer no further dissent.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，虎復擁眾至延綏紅水灘，乞增賞未遂，即縱掠塞外，總兵吳自勉御卻之。

translations.literal: The next autumn the Tiger again led a host to Yansui's Hongshuitan, begged for increased rewards but did not achieve it, and immediately unleashed raiding outside the frontier; regional commander Wu Zimian defended and repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn Hudun Tu again led his followers to Hongshuitan in Yansui. When his demand for increased rewards was denied he immediately raided beyond the frontier. Regional commander Wu Zimian drove him back.

sentences.zh: 既而東附大清兵攻龍門。

translations.literal: Before long he turned east and joined the Great Qing army to attack Longmen.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he threw in his lot with the Great Qing and joined their attack on Longmen.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為大清兵所擊。

translations.literal: Before long he was struck by the Great Qing army.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was defeated by the Great Qing army.

sentences.zh: 六年夏，插漢聞大清兵至，盡驅部眾渡河遠遁。

translations.literal: In the summer of the sixth year, Chakhar, hearing that the Great Qing army had arrived, drove all his followers across the river and fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the sixth year, Chakhar, learning that the Great Qing army was approaching, drove his entire following across the river and fled deep into the steppe.

sentences.zh: 是時，韃靼諸部先後歸附於大清。

translations.literal: At this time the various Tartar divisions successively submitted to the Great Qing.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Tartar tribes were submitting to the Great Qing one after another.

sentences.zh: 明年，大清兵遂大會諸部於兀蘇河南岡，頒軍律焉。

translations.literal: The next year the Great Qing army then assembled the various divisions on the south bank of the Usu River and promulgated military regulations there.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Great Qing army gathered the allied tribes on the south bank of the Usu River and issued them a code of military discipline.

sentences.zh: 而虎已卒，乃追至上都城，盡俘插漢妻孥部眾。

translations.literal: By then Hu had already died; they pursued to Shangdu and captured all of Chakhar's wives, children, and followers.
translations.idiomatic: Hu had already died by then. The Qing forces pursued as far as Shangdu and took captive Chakhar's wives, children, and entire following.

sentences.zh: 其後，套部歲入寧夏、甘、涼境，巡撫陳奇瑜、總兵馬世龍、督師洪承疇等輒擊敗之。

translations.literal: Thereafter the Ordos division entered the territories of Ningxia, Gan, and Liang each year; Grand Coordinator Chen Qiyu, Regional Commander Ma Shilong, Supreme Commander Hong Chengchou, and others repeatedly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the Ordos Mongols raided into Ningxia, Ganzhou, and Liangzhou year after year, and each time Grand Coordinator Chen Qiyu, Regional Commander Ma Shilong, Supreme Commander Hong Chengchou, and others drove them back.

sentences.zh: 套部乾兒罵，亦為總兵尤世祿所斬。

translations.literal: Gan'erma of the Ordos division was also beheaded by Regional Commander You Shilu.
translations.idiomatic: Gan'erma of the Ordos was also killed by Regional Commander You Shilu.

sentences.zh: 迄明世，邊陲無寧，致中原盜賊蜂起。

translations.literal: Throughout the Ming dynasty the frontier knew no peace, which led to bandits rising in swarms in the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the Ming dynasty the frontier never knew peace, and in time bandit armies swarmed across the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 當事者狃與俺答等貢市之便，見插之恣於東也，謂歲捐金錢數十萬，冀苟安旦夕，且覬收之為用，而卒不得。

translations.literal: Those in charge, accustomed to the convenience of tribute markets with Altan and others, seeing Chakhar rampaging in the east, thought that by donating several hundred thousand in gold and cash each year they could secure a brief respite and even hoped to win him over for their use—but in the end they failed.
translations.idiomatic: Officials had grown accustomed to the ease of tribute markets with Altan and his like. When they saw Chakhar running unchecked in the east, they imagined that by paying out several hundred thousand taels each year they could buy a night's peace and perhaps even enlist him on their side—but in the end they achieved neither.

sentences.zh: 迨其後也，明未亡而插先斃，諸部皆折入於大清。

translations.literal: Later, before the Ming perished Chakhar died first, and the various divisions all turned and submitted to the Great Qing.
translations.idiomatic: In time Chakhar died before the Ming dynasty itself fell, and one by one the tribes turned to the Great Qing.

sentences.zh: 國計愈困，邊事愈棘，朝議愈紛，明亦遂不可為矣。

translations.literal: The state's finances grew ever more strained, frontier affairs ever more desperate, court debate ever more chaotic—and the Ming could no longer be saved.
translations.idiomatic: State finances grew tighter, frontier crises multiplied, and court debate grew ever more fractious. The Ming dynasty had reached the point of no return.

sentences.zh: 韃靼地，東至兀良哈，西至瓦剌。

translations.literal: Tartar territory extended east to Uriankhai and west to the Oirats.
translations.idiomatic: Tartar lands stretched east to Uriankhai and west to the Oirat confederation.

sentences.zh: 當洪、永、宣世，國家全盛，頗受戎索，然畔服亦靡常。

translations.literal: During the Hongwu, Yongle, and Xuande reigns the state was at its height and largely held the nomads in check, yet their submission and rebellion were never constant.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hongwu, Yongle, and Xuande reigns the dynasty stood at its zenith and largely kept the steppe peoples in hand, yet their loyalty and defiance were never stable for long.

sentences.zh: 正統後，邊備廢弛，聲靈不振。

translations.literal: After the Zhengtong reign frontier defenses fell into decay and imperial authority no longer carried weight.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhengtong era frontier defenses decayed and the dynasty's authority on the border steadily waned.

sentences.zh: 諸部長多以雄傑之姿，恃其暴強，迭出與中夏抗。

translations.literal: The chieftains of the various divisions, many with the bearing of heroes, relied on their brute strength and came forth in succession to contend with the Central Realm.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal leaders—many of them formidable men in their own right—relied on raw military power and rose one after another to challenge the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 邊境之禍，遂與明終始雲。

translations.literal: Thus frontier calamity ran from the beginning to the end of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier disaster, in short, shadowed the Ming dynasty from first to last.
